events.text: You are very small. In the middle of the night the oil lamp dims, and dims, and a thread of its warmth drifts across the room and into your chest. A voice says, with great satisfaction: "Mm. Lamp oil. Poor, but honest."

choices.text: Ask the voice what it is

effects.log: "Your stomach," it says. "The other one. The one that eats what cannot be eaten." You lie awake until dawn, feeling oddly full.
Under the quilt the voice is muffled and sulky. "I am not a ghost," it says. "Ghosts are thin. I have standards."

choices.text: Call out for someone to bring a light

effects.log: A neighbour relights the lamp, finds it full of oil, and decides you had a dream. The voice, privately, agrees to let her think so.

events.text: A neighbour's ox breaks loose and charges through the yard. You stand frozen. As it thunders past, a warm stream of something leaps from the beast to you, and your legs, all at once, are not frozen at all.

ok.log: You catch the rope and the ox, astonished, stops. The neighbour gives you a persimmon. The voice says the ox tasted of grass and stubbornness.

fail.log: You run faster than any child should, and straight into the fence. The voice apologises: it overestimated the ox. (-5 health)

choices.text: Give the warmth back to the ox

effects.log: You do not know how, but you try, palm on its steaming flank. The ox calms. The voice is baffled. "Nobody gives it back," it says. "Why would anybody give it back?"

events.text: You dream of a mouth as wide as the night sky, open over the mountains, very patient. When you wake, a list glows in front of your eyes: HOST. HUNGER: LOW. FEEDING: BY VICTORY. That is all it says.

effects.log: "Win," says the voice. "Anyone who falls to you leaves something behind: qi, a knack, a scrap of skill. I pick it up. You grow." It sounds very reasonable at six in the morning.

choices.text: Ask what happens if you never win

effects.log: There is a long pause. "Then I get hungry," it says. "And when I am hungry, I eat what is nearest." You do not ask what is nearest. You know.

events.text: A shaman passing through the village stops dead at your gate, rattles a bundle of bells at you, and says that something in you is eating the light. Everyone in the yard looks at you. You look at the shaman's bells, which are, very slowly, going dull.

choices.text: Tell the voice to stop it

effects.log: The bells brighten. The shaman bows, uncertain, and leaves. "It was very good brass," the voice grumbles, for a week.
The shaman ties a red thread round your wrist and tells you to share every meal you ever eat. The voice says this is superstition. It is quieter while you wear the thread.
The shaman goes pale, picks up the bells, and walks very quickly out of the village. The story grows: the child who stares down spirits.

events.text: Your first breakthrough. Your qi turns over like a wheel finding its axle, and something vast turns over with it, stretches, and says: "Good. Now I can eat properly." A new line glows before your eyes: HUNGER.

effects.log: "Names are for things that might leave," it says. Then: "You may call me Taesik. The Great Appetite. Grand, yes?" You call it Tae. It allows this.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants from you

effects.log: "To grow," it says. "Same as you. We are going the same way, host. I am simply louder about dinner."

choices.text: Tell it you are in charge

effects.log: "Of course," it says, with the warmth of a cat agreeing to anything. You feel it smile, somewhere under your ribs.

events.text: An old scroll-seller in the market is selling a cheap tale called The Man Who Ate the Stars. On the cover a cultivator swallows a whirl of light while others fall away from it. The voice, very quietly, says: "Libel."

effects.log: You read it by lamplight. The devourer in it becomes a monster by the last page. The voice spends the night pointing out its many errors of fact. It does not point out the ending.

choices.text: Ask the seller where the story comes from

effects.log: "Old, old," the seller says. "Every hundred years someone is born hungry. It never ends well." The voice says nothing at all, which is worse.

events.text: You realise, one quiet evening, that you have not been alone in your own head since you were five. The voice notices you noticing. "It is not so bad," it offers. "You always have someone to eat with."

effects.log: You laugh until you have to sit down. The voice is pleased. It is the first time it has made a joke on purpose.

choices.text: Ask if it was ever someone

effects.log: "Many someones," it says, after a while. "Every master I ever ate is a little bit in here. That is what devouring is. Remember it, before you take the next one."

events.text: This year the hunger wakes properly. Not in the belly: deeper, behind the navel, where qi pools. You stand in a crowd at the market and feel every person's warmth like the smell of rice from a kitchen.

effects.log: You walk until the crowd is a murmur behind you. The hunger sulks, and grows a little for being refused.

choices.text: Stand there and learn the feeling

effects.log: You stand until you can name it: hungry, not starving; wanting, not taking. Knowing the shape of it helps.

ok.log: The bully who kicks the fruit-seller's basket goes down in the dust. As he falls, a thin warm thread of qi leaves him and comes to you. The hunger purrs.

fail.log: The bully is stronger than he looks. You go home with a split lip and a hunger that laughs at you. (-6 health)

events.text: Your first real fight ends with your opponent on the ground, and something leaves them: a pale stream of light, like breath on a cold morning, that crosses the gap and sinks into your palm. They get up. They are fine. They are a little weaker. You are a little stronger.

effects.log: You lie awake. The voice says, kindly enough, that they will recover their qi in a season. "I only take the loose part," it says. You are not sure it is telling the truth.
It is the best you have ever felt. You practise until the moon is down, just to feel the new warmth move. The voice hums along.

choices.text: Ask the voice what it took

effects.log: "A little qi. A little of how they hold their weight on the back foot," it says. The next morning, you find you hold your weight the same way.

events.text: Supper is rice and cabbage soup. You eat three bowls. You are still hungry. You eat a fourth. The cook stares. The voice says: "That is not the hunger you have to feed, host. That is just you being a growing child."

effects.log: You eat a fifth bowl. The cook tells the whole street. The voice, for once, is embarrassed for you.
You sit with the hunger and let it be a hunger. It is easier than you thought. The cook takes the fifth bowl home, relieved.

events.text: A wild boar comes down into the millet field. Everyone runs for sticks. The hunger sits up very straight.

ok.log: The boar turns, stumbles and flees into the woods, and as it goes a bright current of beast-qi follows you instead of it. The farmers cheer. You feel like you swallowed a bonfire.

fail.log: The boar knocks you flat and runs off with half the millet. The hunger is very rude about it. (-10 health)

choices.text: Help drive it off with the others

effects.log: Twenty people with sticks and pots drive the boar off. Nothing comes to you. The hunger grumbles, but you feel oddly proud of your village.

events.text: Ding. A new line glows: HUNGER WILL RISE EVERY YEAR. FEED IT BY VICTORY, BY TREASURE, BY POINTS. IF NOT FED, IT FEEDS ON THE HOST. The voice adds, rather quickly: "That last line is standard wording. Very rarely applies."

effects.log: "Rarely," it says. "Hardly ever. Mostly never. Please train." You go and train.

choices.text: Promise yourself you will stay its master

effects.log: You make the promise out loud, in the yard, to nobody. The voice listens very carefully. It does not say whether it believes you.

events.text: You win a sparring bout against a friend, laughing, and the hunger reaches for them before you can think. You feel the thread of their qi start to lift toward you, like steam from a cup.

effects.log: You clench something inside you that has no name and the thread falls back. It hurts like biting your tongue. Your friend asks why you have gone white. (-4 health)
Just a little. Your friend yawns, and says they are tired, suddenly. You walk home quite fast.

events.text: A peddler sells you a dried spirit herb, cheap, for a cough you do not have. The hunger notices it in your sleeve and goes very quiet, the way a dog goes quiet near a kitchen door.

choices.text: Let the System devour the herb

effects.log: You hold it in your palm and it dissolves into green light and is gone. The hunger settles like a cat in the sun. So that is how treasures taste.

choices.text: Brew it for a sick neighbour

effects.log: The old neighbour drinks it and sleeps easier. The hunger watches the steam go with great longing, and says nothing.

events.text: A great master passes through town in a palanquin. You can feel their qi from the end of the street: deep, old, like a well a hundred years deep. The hunger says, very softly: "One of those would feed us for ten years."

effects.log: You walk the other way until the feeling fades. The voice says nothing for a day, which is how it apologises.
You watch. You do not move. That night you dream of drinking from a well with no bottom, and wake ashamed and hungrier.

choices.text: Ask how a master could even be beaten

effects.log: The voice explains, step by careful step. It has clearly thought about it a great deal. You are frightened by how much sense it makes.

events.text: You win a fight and, as your foe's qi drains toward you in a bright thread, you see their face. Not pain. Fear. As if they had heard stories, and you were one.

effects.log: You stop it. The light falls back into them like water into a cup. They stare at you, then run. The hunger is furious. You feel cleaner than you have in years.
You finish it. They will recover, in a season or two. You tell yourself that several times on the walk home.

choices.text: Tell them it will grow back

effects.log: "It grows back," you say. They do not believe you. You are not sure you believe yourself.

events.text: You catch yourself, in a crowded teahouse, sorting the people by flavour. That one tastes of iron. That one of plum blossom. That one is thin and sour, not worth the effort.

choices.text: Leave and sit by the river

effects.log: You sit by the river until people are people again. It takes all afternoon.

choices.text: Ask the voice to stop doing that

effects.log: "I am not doing it," the voice says, quietly. "You are." You do not sleep well.
You finish your tea. The plum-blossom one smiles at you on the way out. You smile back, and wish you had not thought of them that way.

events.text: A wounded cultivator lies at the side of the road, unconscious, qi leaking out of them like heat from a cooling stove. Nobody is coming. The hunger says: "It is going to waste anyway."

choices.text: Carry them to the nearest doctor

effects.log: You carry them ten li. The doctor saves them. The hunger grinds its teeth all the way, which turns out to be a very good reason to walk faster. (-3 health)

choices.text: Gather only the qi already spilt

effects.log: You take only what is drifting loose in the air, not a thread more, and then you bind their wound. It is the first time the hunger has ever been made to wait at the table.

choices.text: Take what is left in them

effects.log: It is very easy. They are still breathing when you leave. You do not look back, and later you wish you had.

events.text: In a dream you are enormous, and you are eating a sect: its lanterns, its training yard, the warm qi of a hundred disciples, the way a fire eats a field. You wake up with the sheet in your fists.

choices.text: Get up and train until dawn

effects.log: You train until your arms shake, until all you are is tired. The dream does not come back that year.
You tell a friend over breakfast, as a joke. They laugh. Saying it out loud makes it smaller. That helps.

choices.text: Lie still and listen to the voice

effects.log: "That was not me," it says. "That was you, hungry. There is a difference, host. Try to keep it."

events.text: A notorious demonic cultivator is caught by the town guard and chained in the square for the magistrate. Their qi is thick and black and rich. The voice says: "Nobody would mind. Nobody would even notice."

ok.log: They break a chain and come at you, and lose. Their dark qi comes to you in a slow, heavy stream, like ink poured into water. It sits in you for a month, sour.

fail.log: Chained or not, they are far better than you. You crawl away before the guard comes. (-12 health)

effects.log: Justice is slow and boring and not yours. The hunger calls you a fool. You sleep better than it does.

events.text: An offer, at last, from the voice: "Host, there is an elder in the next valley who has hidden away from the world for fifty years. Fifty years of qi. Nobody knows he is there. Just one."

effects.log: "No." It is the shortest word you know and the hardest. The voice goes quiet. You think, for a moment, that it is relieved.
You find the hut. You see an old man watering beans. You go home without a word. You never tell the voice why.

choices.text: Ask the voice why it wants him

effects.log: "Because I am a hunger," it says. "Wanting is what I am. Refusing is what you are for."

events.text: Your stolen strength has carried you further than you ever hoped. Tonight, alone, you wonder how much of you is still you: your stance came from a bandit, your breath from a hermit, your nerve from a tiger.

choices.text: Make a list of what is yours

effects.log: Kindness, stubbornness, a bad singing voice, a habit of laughing at the wrong time. The list is long enough. You sleep.
A river is still a river, whatever streams run into it. You choose to believe that. Some days you even do.

events.text: The hunger offers you something new: if you devour a whole lifetime of a master's art, every stance and every breath, you would be at the peak in a single night. All you need is a master who loses.

choices.text: Refuse and train the slow way

effects.log: Slow is a strange luxury for a devourer. You spend a whole season on a single stance, and own every part of it.

choices.text: Hunt for a master who deserves it

effects.log: Only the cruel ones, you tell yourself. Only the ones the world would not miss. You start a list. It is a long one, which is its own kind of horror.

events.text: You beat three road bandits in a row. The voice reviews them, one by one, like a teahouse critic. "First: watery. Second: watery, with a note of fear. Third: I do not wish to speak of the third."

effects.log: "They were doing their best," you say. "Their best," the voice says, "was boiled millet without salt." The bandits, who cannot hear any of this, are glad to be alive.

choices.text: Ask what a good meal tastes like

effects.log: It describes, at length and with real feeling, the qi of a mountain master: pine resin, cold springs, a hint of old iron. You find you are starving.

events.text: Ding. A complaint has been lodged. The System notes, formally, that the host has eaten nothing but bandits, drunks and one very angry goose for three years, and requests "something with flavour".

ok.log: The graduate draws with a flourish and lands on the ground with a different flourish. The voice sighs with pleasure. "Finally. Proper technique. Notes of sword oil and arrogance."

fail.log: The graduate is quite good, actually. The voice files a second complaint, this time about you. (-8 health)

choices.text: Tell it the goose was delicious

effects.log: "The goose," says the voice, with feeling, "was the only one who fought with conviction." You have to admit this is true.

events.text: You are sated, and the System has opinions about being sated. It wants to tell you about every meal of the year, in order, with ratings. It is very pleased. It is extremely boring.

effects.log: It takes three evenings. The tiger gets nine out of ten. The magistrate's nephew gets two. You fall asleep during the summary, and it does not mind.
"Good year," it says, sulkily. Then, after a while, unable to help itself: "The tiger, though."

events.text: A drunk picks a fight with you in an inn. It is not a fight. The voice says: "I am not eating that. I will not. Host, I have a reputation."

effects.log: You carry the drunk upstairs and put a blanket on them. The innkeeper gives you free soup. The voice says it will eat the soup, at least.

ok.log: You simply hold their wrist until they fall asleep standing. The inn applauds. The voice says this was "tasteful".

fail.log: The drunk headbutts you by accident and then apologises at length. Nobody devours anybody. (-3 health)

events.text: You finally beat a Buddhist monk in a friendly bout at a temple fair, and the voice makes a face you can feel. "Vegetables," it says. "Thirty years of vegetables. The qi tastes of tofu. Pure, wholesome, unforgivable tofu."

effects.log: The monk laughs, says they felt nothing leave but their pride, and invites you to lunch. It is, of course, tofu. The voice is in despair.

choices.text: Tell the voice tofu is good for it

effects.log: "I do not need to be good," says the voice. "I need to be full." But your qi runs very clean and calm for a month afterwards, and it grudgingly admits it.

events.text: A poison master tries to kill you at dinner. You feel the poison settle, and the System... eats it. "Oh," it says, surprised. "Oh, that is spicy. Host. Host, can we find more poison masters?"

choices.text: Go and find the poison master

ok.log: You find them in the stables, astonished you are standing. They lose quickly. Their qi tastes, the System reports, "like chilli in a cold winter". You learn a good deal about poisons.

fail.log: The poison master was also a sword master. You escape with a long cut and a System that keeps asking if you are going back. (-10 health)

effects.log: "Fine," it says. "Fine. It was very good, though." You change inns.

events.text: You are hungry, and the voice is not funny when it is hungry. It is quiet and polite and keeps mentioning, very lightly, how plump and slow the people in the market look today.

choices.text: Buy it a beast core to shut it up

effects.log: A hunter sells you a beast core, warm and red as an ember. The voice stops mentioning the market. It does not stop looking at the core.

choices.text: Tell it that is not funny

effects.log: "I was not joking," it says. Then, after a moment: "Sorry. Hungry." It is the first time it has ever said sorry.

choices.text: Go and pick a fight with a bandit gang

ok.log: The gang loses, loudly. The voice eats, and is funny again by evening, and bitterly critical of the gang's diet.

fail.log: There were more of them than you counted. You limp home. The voice is very quiet and very polite all the way. (-8 health)

events.text: A cook in the market sells skewers of grilled spirit-mushroom, faintly glowing. The System, which has never once cared about ordinary food, asks, very shyly, if you could try one. "For research."

effects.log: It is excellent. The voice is quiet for a long time, and then says, "So that is what the fuss was about." It asks about skewers every year after that.

choices.text: Tell the System it does not have a tongue

effects.log: "I have yours," it says, wounded. You buy one skewer, out of guilt.

events.text: Ding. The System has prepared a list, "The Ten Most Disappointing Things the Host Has Defeated", and would like to read it aloud. Number one is a scarecrow you once attacked by mistake in the dark.

effects.log: Number four is a famous young master. Number seven is a cabbage. You laugh until you cry, and you feel, for once, like the two of you are friends.

choices.text: Insist the scarecrow was a real threat

effects.log: "It had no qi," the voice says. "It had straw." "It had intent," you say. You argue happily for an hour.

events.text: A noble young master at a banquet boasts of the rare Golden Crane Soup that strengthens qi. The System leans forward, interested. Then it tastes a spoonful through you and says, "It is chicken. It is just chicken."

effects.log: "It is very fine chicken," you say. The cook in the doorway nods slowly. The young master stops inviting you to things.
You praise the soup. The System sulks. The young master thinks you are very refined.

events.text: You throw a kick in practice and {npc}, a weathered martial instructor who has seen ten thousand kicks, stops talking. "That is the Black Wind Gang's Turning Heel," {he} says. "I know. They broke my wrist with it. Where did you learn it?"

effects.log: {npc} nods slowly and does not believe a word. "Then the stranger was a Black Wind man," {he} says. "Be careful who you keep company with."

choices.text: Say you picked it up in a fight

effects.log: "In a fight," {npc} repeats. "You see a kick once and keep it." {He} looks at you for a long time. "That is either genius or something I should worry about."
{npc} lets it go. But from that day {he} watches your practice, every day, from the shade of the gate.

events.text: {npc} has made a list. Every move you have used this year, and where it comes from: a bandit chief's elbow, a hunter's footwork, a wandering swordsman's draw. Next to each one, a date. Next to each date, a fight you won.

effects.log: You tell {him} everything. {npc} is quiet for so long that you start to worry. Then {he} says: "So that is why the Black Wind man stopped fighting after you. I had wondered."
{npc} burns it, in front of you. "I can still remember it," {he} says. "I only burned the paper. Do not make me write another one."
You leave. {npc} does not follow. You lie awake wondering who else has started making lists.

events.text: {npc} comes to you with tea and a proposal. "If you can take a technique, can you give one back? My best student lost their footwork to a fever. I have tried everything."

ok.log: You sit with the student, palms together, and slowly let a borrowed stream of footwork flow out of you and into them. It works. {npc} turns away so you will not see {his} face. (-5 qi)

fail.log: It does not go out the way it came in. The hunger clamps down on it. You apologise. {npc} says it was worth trying, and means it. (-5 health)

effects.log: "Only takes," {npc} says. "Then it is not a gift. It is a debt. Remember who you owe."

events.text: A wandering swordsman you beat two years ago finds you on the road. "You use my draw," they say flatly. "The one my teacher taught me. The one I have not been able to do since you."

roll.foeName: The swordsman whose draw you took

ok.log: You win again, and the hunger takes another sip of light from them before you can stop it. They walk away without a word. You feel heavier, not stronger.

fail.log: They win, and stand over you, and do not take anything, because they cannot. "Keep it," they say. "Use it well. It was a good draw." (-9 health)

choices.text: Apologise and teach them a new one

effects.log: You teach them a stance you devoured from a bandit, honestly earned by them now. It is not their teacher's draw. They take it, and bow, and go.

events.text: At a tournament, three elders on the judges' bench lean together. Your second bout used a palm strike from the southern coast. Your third used a staff form from the northern passes. You are from neither.

choices.text: Win with only your own art

ok.log: For the final, you use nothing borrowed. Just your stubborn, ordinary, home-grown form. You win anyway. The elders stop whispering and start taking notes.

fail.log: Your own art is not enough, today. You lose the final with dignity. The elders decide you are only a talented copycat, which is safer. (-6 health)

effects.log: You win with a dozen schools' worth of moves. The crowd roars. The elders do not. One of them, in orthodox white, writes your name very carefully in a small black book.

events.text: A street child who watches every fight in the market has started to copy you. "How do you do the bandit kick and the monk palm in the same breath?" they demand. "Nobody learns both."

choices.text: Teach the child the kick, properly

effects.log: It takes a month. The child earns it, the slow way, every bruise. You have never been prouder of anything you did not devour.

choices.text: Say you are just very talented

effects.log: "Liar," says the child, cheerfully, and follows you for a week trying to catch you at it.

events.text: {npc} is old now and sends for you. "I kept watching," {he} says. "All these years. You took a lot. But you never took from anyone who was down for good. I wanted you to know that somebody saw."

effects.log: You sit with {him} until evening. {npc} falls asleep in the chair, the old list of your stolen moves on {his} knee, every line crossed out.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what you should do now

effects.log: "Give some of it back," {npc} says. "Teach. A thief who teaches is a strange kind of master. The world has room for one."

events.text: You catch yourself breathing in a pattern you never learned, a slow tidal breath from someone you beat years ago. You have forgotten their face. Their breath is still in you, every morning.

choices.text: Find out who it belonged to

effects.log: It takes a season of asking. They were a pearl diver who took up the sword late. You visit their village and leave a gift on the step, nameless.
You practise it until it has your rhythm and nobody else's. It is still a debt. It is also, now, yours.

events.text: A martial scholar is writing an encyclopaedia of techniques and wants to interview you, because, they say, you seem to know "a little of everything, in the hands of nobody in particular".

effects.log: You tell them about each technique as if you had studied it. The scholar is delighted and puts you in a footnote: a remarkable eclectic. The voice wants a bigger footnote.
You decline. The scholar is disappointed but writes, in the margin of their notes, a single question mark beside your name.

events.text: {npc}, an inspector of the Orthodox Alliance in spotless white, stops you at the town gate. "Three fighters you defeated this year lost a season of qi each," {he} says. "That is the mark of the Marrow-Draining Art. Explain."

choices.text: Say they were simply beaten badly

effects.log: "Badly," {npc} repeats, writing. "Of course." {He} lets you through. {He} does not stop writing.

choices.text: Offer to have your meridians examined

ok.log: {npc} presses two fingers to your wrist for a long time. The System holds perfectly still, like a child hiding in a cupboard. "Clean," {npc} says at last, frowning. "Strangely clean."

fail.log: {npc}'s fingers find something under your pulse: a slow pull, like a tide. {He} lets go fast. "I will be watching you," {he} says.

effects.log: {npc} does not stop you. That is somehow worse. You hear, behind you, a brush on paper.

events.text: A notice is pinned to the wall of the town hall. It does not name you. It describes a young fighter of your build who "drinks the qi of the fallen" and asks the righteous to report any sighting to the Alliance.

effects.log: You tear it down. By noon there are two more. Someone has a very good copyist.

choices.text: Leave it, and stop fighting in public

effects.log: You train in the hills now, alone. The hunger hates the quiet. The notice yellows in the rain.

ok.log: A clerk, for a cup of wine, tells you: the inspector in white wrote it, and has written to three sects about you.

fail.log: Asking about the notice is, it turns out, a very good way to make people look at it more closely.

events.text: {npc} has brought witnesses: two sect disciples you beat last spring, both still pale. They point at you in the square. "After we fell," one says, "we felt something leave. Like warm water draining out of a bath."

choices.text: Admit it, and swear you take no lives

effects.log: The square goes silent. {npc} looks at you a long while. "An honest demon," {he} says. "I have never met one. I am not sure it exists." But {he} does not draw a sword.

ok.log: You are calm and reasonable and very convincing. The witnesses begin to doubt themselves. {npc} does not.

fail.log: Your denial is too smooth. The crowd decides at once. Doors close as you walk home.

choices.text: Offer the disciples your own qi back

effects.log: You lay a palm on each and push warmth into them until you are dizzy. Colour comes back to their faces. {npc} watches, and for the first time, {his} brush stops. (-10 qi)

events.text: {npc} has come with a writ and four Alliance swords. "Submit to the sealing of your dantian," {he} says, "or be treated as a demonic cultivator."

ok.log: You win. As {npc} falls, the hunger reaches and takes a stream of pure, cold orthodox qi. {He} looks up at you as it goes, and you see that you have just proved {him} right.

fail.log: {npc} is very good. You escape over a wall, qi spilling, with an Alliance writ on your name. (-14 health)

effects.log: The sealing needles go in. The hunger screams. Then, slowly, it finds a way round them, as water does. The seal holds for a year. {npc} is, oddly, gentle about it. (-15 qi)

ok.log: You are over the roofs before the swords are drawn. Behind you {npc} does not shout. {He} simply watches you go and writes it down.

fail.log: You get away, just, with a cut on your arm and a name in the Alliance's book. (-8 health)

events.text: {npc} finds you again, alone this time, without a writ. "I have been reading," {he} says. "The old records. The Marrow-Draining Art always rots its user from the inside. You do not seem rotten. Why not?"

choices.text: Say you feed it only on the guilty

effects.log: {npc} sits on a stone. "Then you are a judge," {he} says. "That is my job. We should talk about who is guilty." You talk until dark.

choices.text: Say it is not the same art

effects.log: You explain the System as well as you can. {npc} listens to every word. "A hunger with a ledger," {he} says. "That is worse, or better. I do not know yet."
You show {him} your thin wrists, your lean years. {npc} goes quiet. "Then I will not hurry it," {he} says, and for the first time puts away the brush.

events.text: A real demonic sect hears the rumours and sends an envoy with a letter of welcome. "One of us," it says, in beautiful calligraphy. "Come home. We will feed you better than the righteous ever will."

effects.log: You burn it. The hunger watches the smoke and sighs. "They would have fed us," it says. "They would have owned us," you say.

choices.text: Meet the envoy, out of curiosity

effects.log: The envoy is charming, polite, and very interested in exactly how much you can eat. You leave with an invitation, a headache and no promise.

choices.text: Beat the envoy for the insult

ok.log: The envoy loses. Their qi is dark, rich and slightly bitter, like over-steeped tea. The Alliance, oddly, hears of it and thinks better of you.

fail.log: The envoy laughs, wipes their blade, and leaves the letter on your chest. "The offer stands," it says. (-10 health)

events.text: The Alliance has a mirror, an old bronze one, that is said to show any demonic art as a black smoke. Every candidate at the great tournament must look into it. You are next in line.

ok.log: In the mirror there is no smoke. There is only a faint violet mouth, smiling, very small, which nobody else seems to see. You pass.

fail.log: The mirror clouds. Not black: violet. The judges argue for an hour about whether violet counts. You are disqualified "pending review".

effects.log: You withdraw, pleading an injury. The voice is disappointed; tournaments are its favourite buffet.

events.text: {npc} has been wounded by a real demonic master and lies in a borrowed room, qi poisoned and turning black. The doctors say only someone who can draw qi out could pull the poison from {him}.

effects.log: You lay your palms on {npc} and let the hunger eat only the poison, black thread by black thread. It tastes foul. When {he} wakes {he} looks at you for a long time. "Huh," {he} says. (-10 health)
You leave. The doctors do their best. {npc} lives, slowly, and is never quite as quick again. You hear about it and are not sure what you feel.

events.text: {npc} stands before the Alliance council with a stack of records and asks, publicly, that the Alliance's mark on your name be lifted. "I have watched this one for years," {he} says. "It is a hunger. It is not a demon."

effects.log: The council argues for a day. The mark is lifted, "provisionally". {npc} buys you a cup of tea afterwards and says it is the first time {he} has ever argued for anyone.
You send a letter of thanks. The mark is lifted without you. Someone in the council mutters that the hungry one did not even come.

events.text: An orthodox sect master you have never met declares, before a crowd, that you are the Heaven-Devouring Demon of the old prophecy and must be destroyed before you reach the peak. The crowd looks at you.

choices.text: Challenge the master to a public duel

roll.foeName: The sect master who named you

ok.log: You win, before a thousand people. The master's qi comes to you like spring meltwater. Half the crowd now thinks the prophecy is true. The other half thinks it should be.

fail.log: You lose, before a thousand people. The master lets you walk away, which is its own kind of insult. (-14 health)

choices.text: Laugh and say you are much too hungry for prophecies

effects.log: The crowd laughs with you. Some of them. The master does not. But a prophecy that gets a laugh loses something it never quite gets back.

choices.text: Leave the province for a few years

effects.log: You go somewhere nobody has heard of the old prophecy. It takes a while to find such a place.

events.text: In a bad year, the hunger drives you to take more than you should from a defeated foe in front of witnesses. They see the light stream out of the fallen fighter. Someone screams the word: demon.

effects.log: You stay. You explain. You help the fallen fighter up and give them rice money. The word demon follows you anyway, but now it has a question mark.
You run. By morning the story has you eating the fighter whole. It is wildly wrong, and it is everywhere.

events.text: You have found the switch: a way to hold the hunger back, so a beaten foe walks away whole. Holding it is like holding your breath under water. The voice asks, politely, how long you intend to do this.

choices.text: Say as long as I need to

effects.log: "Then I will wait," it says. "I am very good at waiting. I am a hunger." That is not reassuring.
"Friends," says the voice. "How many friends do you plan to have?" More, you decide, out of spite.

events.text: You have held the hunger back for a full year. Your foes have walked away whole. You are thinner, slower, and your qi tastes, the voice informs you, "like an empty bowl".

effects.log: You keep holding. Something in you grows that is not the hunger: a muscle, the voice calls it, with grudging respect. (-5 health)

ok.log: You let go, only for that one fight, only for a bully who deserved it. The relief is so huge it frightens you.

fail.log: You let go and still lose. The hunger is beside itself with rage. (-8 health)

events.text: A sect that you are visiting is attacked by raiders. You could hold the hunger back and fight as yourself, fairly, or let go and be terrible.

ok.log: You fight hard and fair and plain. You win, just. Nobody looks at you afterwards with fear, only gratitude. It is a new feeling.

fail.log: Fair is not enough tonight. You are knocked down, and the sect's own elders finish the raiders. They carry you in. (-12 health)

ok.log: You let go. Light streams to you from the raiders' captain like a river into the sea. The raid breaks in a breath. The sect thanks you, from a careful distance.

fail.log: Even terrible, you are outmatched. You crawl back behind the sect's wall, empty. (-14 health)

events.text: A small monastery teaches a breathing exercise for monks who cannot stop eating. You go, half joking, and find that it works on the other hunger too.

choices.text: Stay a season and learn it

effects.log: Breathe in for four, hold for four, let the wanting pass through like weather. The hunger is outraged to find itself, for whole hours, quite calm.

choices.text: Learn the first part and leave

effects.log: You learn enough to take the edge off. The abbot says you will be back. You are, years later.

events.text: You beat a rival school's prodigy in a hard bout. You have the hunger leashed. The prodigy's qi hangs in the air between you, loose and bright, and the System begs.

effects.log: It fades back into the prodigy, who stands and bows, whole. They never know how close it was. The voice does not speak to you for a week.
A sip. A taste. Not enough to hurt them. Enough to remember that you could have taken the whole cup.

events.text: Ding. The System, with great formality, presents you with a figure: if you had devoured every fight in the last three years, you would be a full realm higher now. It does not say anything else. It does not need to.

effects.log: "Worth what?" it asks, genuinely. You try to explain. It listens. Afterwards it says, "I still do not understand. But I wrote it down."

choices.text: Ask it to stop keeping that figure

effects.log: "I cannot," it says. "I am a ledger as well as a mouth. But I will not read it to you again." It keeps its word, mostly.
You feel it: a whole realm, given away, one fight at a time. It hurts more than you thought.

events.text: The hunger is very loud this year. You feel it pulling at everyone you pass. Holding it back takes everything. One night you realise you have held it so tightly that your own qi has stopped moving.

effects.log: You let the hunger breathe without letting it eat. A leash, not a noose. It quiets, a little, and so do you.
You hold until your hands shake. Something in your chest goes cold and still for a month. The hunger is afraid of you, briefly. (-8 health)

events.text: An old master who once held a devouring art of their own, and broke it, offers you advice over a game of go: "Do not starve it. Do not stuff it. Feed it at the same hour, the same amount, like a horse."

effects.log: You set a rhythm: one fight a season, one treasure a year, never more. The hunger grumbles and then, astonishingly, settles.

choices.text: Ask how they broke their art

effects.log: "I gave it everything I had," the old master says, "so it had nothing left to want." They place a stone. They have lost every game of go for forty years, they say, quite happily.

events.text: A bully half your strength picks a fight. You could end it in one breath and feed well. You are sated, and the voice is too lazy to care which you choose.

ok.log: One breath. Down. A wisp of thin qi drifts to you. "Dessert," the voice says, sleepily.

fail.log: You were too relaxed. The bully gets one in. You end it after that, embarrassed. (-5 health)

effects.log: You walk away. The bully claims a victory to everyone in the street. You find you do not mind at all. Being full is a kind of freedom.

events.text: At a crossroads inn you feel it before you see {npc}: another hunger, across the room, sniffing the air the way yours does. {npc} looks up at the same moment, and smiles very slowly. "Oh," {he} says. "There are two of us."

effects.log: You talk all night. {npc} has a voice in {his} head too, and it is, {he} says, "a terrible snob about bandits". You laugh at the same moments. It frightens you both.
You leave. {npc} watches you go. Your voice says, very quietly, "That one could eat us." For once you agree.
"Another host," it says. "Another System. Crimson, not violet. We are not friends." {npc} raises {his} cup to you across the room.

events.text: {npc} turns up at the same bandit fortress you came to clear. Two devourers, one meal. {He} grins. "Shall we race?"

ok.log: You clear the east wall before {npc} clears the west. {He} is annoyed and delighted at once. "Next time," {he} says.

fail.log: {npc} is faster. By the time you reach the hall, {he} is sitting on the bandit chief's chair, glowing faintly, smug as a cat.

effects.log: You split the gang down the middle. {npc} is surprised by fairness. "Is that a rule you have?" {he} asks. "I am trying it," you say.

events.text: {npc} has been eating well. Too well. Villages near {his} road speak of fighters left pale and weak for years. {He} comes to visit you, glowing with stolen qi, and asks why you look so thin.

effects.log: "Slow down," {npc} repeats, as if you had suggested {he} stop breathing. "Why would I? Look at me." You do. {He} looks wonderful, and you are afraid.
"Like being a god," {npc} says simply. Your own hunger listens to every word, very still.

ok.log: A friendly bout. You both keep your hungers leashed, barely. You win on technique. {npc} stares at you. "How are you this good, eating so little?"

fail.log: {npc} wins easily, and while you are down you feel {his} hunger sniff at you, and turn away. "Too thin," {he} says, kindly. (-8 health)

events.text: Word comes that {npc} has devoured a whole sect's elders in a single night. The Alliance is mustering. Your own voice says, very carefully: "Host, if one of us is to eat the other, it had better be us."

ok.log: On a burning hillside you beat {npc}, and the crimson hunger pours out of {him} toward you, an ocean of it. You take only enough to leave {him} empty and alive. {He} weeps, which no devourer does.

fail.log: {npc} beats you, and stands over you, and the crimson hunger sniffs at you, and turns away. "Not you," {he} says. "Not yet." (-18 health)

effects.log: You leave it. The Alliance hunts {npc} for three years and catches nothing but rumours. You hear each one.

events.text: {npc} writes to you from far away. "You were right," the letter says. "It does not stop. I have started to eat my own years. How do you hold it? Tell me how you hold it."

effects.log: You write ten pages: the breathing, the rhythm, the switch, the shame. Months later a single line comes back. "It is working. I hate you." You laugh out loud.
You travel a month to sit beside {npc} through a bad winter, both your hungers howling, neither of you eating. In spring {he} can hold it alone. (-4 health)

events.text: {npc} turns up on your doorstep, empty and gentle, years after the burning hill. "I have nothing left to devour with," {he} says. "Do you need someone to sweep the yard?"

effects.log: {npc} sweeps the yard every morning. Sometimes, at dusk, you catch {him} looking at the hills where the bandits live, and then back at the broom, and smiling.
{npc} takes the money and bows deeply. A year later you hear of a quiet teacher in a hill village, very patient with hungry children.
{npc} goes without arguing. You watch {him} out of sight and feel your own hunger watch too.

events.text: {npc} comes back stronger than ever. "I have eaten a hundred," {he} says. "You have eaten, what, thirty? Let us see whose System is the better cook."

ok.log: It is the hardest fight of your life. At the end {npc} is on one knee and {his} crimson hunger, unbelievably, gives way to yours. You take only a little. Enough to end it.

fail.log: {npc} wins. {He} does not devour you. "I want you to see me win again," {he} says, which is worse. (-16 health)

effects.log: "I am not a dish," you say. {npc} laughs, honestly, and goes to look for someone who is.

events.text: You and {npc} sit on a roof with a pot of barley tea, two hosts with two voices, comparing notes. Yours is a snob about bandits. {His} voice is afraid of the dark. Neither of you knows where they came from.

effects.log: A dead god's appetite, split in two. A curse. A clerk in heaven who lost a ledger. You make up theories until dawn and like the clerk best.

choices.text: Promise to stop each other, if it comes to that

effects.log: You shake on it, solemn and a little giddy. {npc} says it is the nicest thing anyone has ever promised {him}.

events.text: {npc} lies dying of old age, and the crimson hunger in {him} is restless, looking for somewhere to go next. "Do not let it go into a child," {he} whispers. "Take it, if you can. Or end it."

effects.log: You lay your hand on {npc}'s chest and the crimson light comes into you, slow, enormous. Your violet hunger meets it, and swallows it, and is quiet for a long time. {npc} smiles and closes {his} eyes.

choices.text: Help it fade into the air

effects.log: With everything you learned of holding, you hold the crimson hunger until it thins into morning mist. {npc} watches it go, and laughs, softly, like someone set down a heavy load.

events.text: A young cultivator stops you on the road. "You are the one the crimson devourer used to talk about," they say. "I have a voice too. It just woke up. It is so hungry. What do I do?"

effects.log: You teach them the switch, the breath, the rhythm, the shame and the mercy. They learn fast. Your own voice watches, and does not complain once.

choices.text: Give them a beast core and some advice

effects.log: "Feed it this. Then go and find a monastery with a breathing exercise. Then write to me." They write every year.

events.text: The sect's treasure hall keeps a Spirit Essence Pearl, the last of its kind, saved for the day the patriarch's illness turns. You walk past it on guard duty. The hunger stops in the doorway and will not move.

effects.log: You walk on, one step at a time, like pulling a mule. The hunger howls inside you all night.
You step inside and look. The pearl is the colour of milk and moonlight. You leave. You think about it every day.

events.text: It is a starving year, and you are on guard duty again, alone, at midnight. The pearl glows. The hunger has stopped talking. It is just pulling, steadily, like a current.

effects.log: You hold it in your palm. It turns to white light and pours into you like moonlight into a well. For the first time in years the hunger is utterly silent. The stand is empty.

choices.text: Ask to be taken off the duty

effects.log: You ask, white-faced, for any other duty. The elder looks at you curiously and sends you to the kitchens. The kitchens are bad too, but bearable. (-4 health)

choices.text: Sit by the pearl till dawn and eat nothing

effects.log: You sit there all night, an arm's length from it. At dawn you are shaking and the pearl is still on its stand. It is the strongest thing you have ever done. (-6 health)

events.text: The patriarch's illness turns. {npc}, the old treasure elder, unlocks the hall with shaking hands and finds the stand empty. {He} turns, very slowly, and looks at every disciple on the steps. {His} eyes stop on you.

effects.log: You kneel and tell {npc} everything. {He} is silent for a long time. "Then you carry the patriarch's life in you," {he} says. "Find a way to give it back."

ok.log: {npc}'s eyes move on. The sect blames a thief from outside. You hear the word thief all year and flinch every time.

fail.log: {npc} sees it on your face before you can hide it. "You," {he} says, quietly, and the whole sect hears it.

events.text: The patriarch is fading. {npc} asks you, plainly: "You took the pearl's essence. Can you give it back? Even part?"

choices.text: Pour your own qi into the patriarch

effects.log: You sit by the patriarch for nine days, palms on the old chest, giving back moonlight a thread at a time. On the tenth day the patriarch sits up and asks for porridge. You are grey and thin and happier than in years. (-20 qi)

choices.text: Go and find another treasure for the patriarch

ok.log: Three months in the high passes and you come back with a thousand-year ginseng, and you do not let the hunger near it. The patriarch lives. {npc} bows to you.

fail.log: You search the mountains for a season and find nothing. The patriarch lingers on, weakly. {npc} does not blame you to your face. (-10 health)

events.text: Your sect is preparing a great spirit-gathering formation to break through its oldest master. At its heart sits a Beast Core the size of a fist. The hunger looks at it the way a dog looks at a roast on a feast day.

ok.log: You guard it for forty days and never let the hunger touch it. The master breaks through. The sect gives you a small core of your own, as thanks, and you let the hunger have that one.

fail.log: On the thirty-ninth night you nod off, and wake to find a thin stream of light running from the core into your palm. You pull away in horror. The formation still works, barely. Nobody knows why it was weaker.

choices.text: Ask to be sent away until it is over

effects.log: You go on a long errand to the coast. When you come back, the master has broken through and the core is gone. The hunger is in a sulk for a year.

events.text: An enemy sect has stolen your sect's spirit spring stone, the heart of its training grounds. The elders are planning a raid. You could go in first, alone, and devour your way through.

ok.log: You go through the enemy gate like water through sand, and a stream of light follows you from every guard you beat. You come back with the stone. The elders thank you and stand, just slightly, further away.

fail.log: You get as far as the second courtyard. The elders' raid saves you, and the stone, and you lie in the infirmary listening to them argue about you. (-16 health)

choices.text: Go in with the elders, leashed

effects.log: You fight beside your elders and take nothing from anyone. The raid succeeds. For once you are just a disciple among disciples. It is wonderful.

events.text: The sect's alchemist brings you a problem: a pill furnace has gone wrong, and the half-made pill inside is boiling with wild qi that could crack the whole hall. "I hear you can eat that kind of thing," the alchemist whispers.

effects.log: You put both hands on the furnace and drink. It is hot, bitter, and wonderful. The hall stops shaking. The alchemist stares at you, then at the empty furnace, then writes something down very fast. (-5 health)

ok.log: You open the vents in the right order and the qi drains out over the roof as harmless green fire. The alchemist names a technique after you, badly.

fail.log: The furnace bursts. Nobody is badly hurt, but your eyebrows take a season to grow back. (-8 health)

events.text: Years later, {npc} is dying and calls for you. "I never told anyone about the pearl," {he} says. "I told them it was a thief. I wanted to see what kind of person you would become. Tell me."

effects.log: You tell {him} all of it: the hunger, the leash, the bad years and the good. {npc} listens to the end. "Good enough," {he} says. "Good enough is a great deal."

choices.text: Say you are still finding out

effects.log: {npc} laughs, a dry old laugh. "That is the right answer," {he} says. "The others all lied."

events.text: You find, in a ruined shrine, an Essence Pearl wrapped in old silk. A brush note on the silk asks the finder to carry it to a sect that has not existed for two hundred years.

effects.log: You fold the silk and put the pearl in your pack. The hunger is beside itself with joy. You keep the note too, and are not sure why.

ok.log: A farmer in a far valley turns out to be the last of the line. You give the farmer the pearl. The farmer weeps, and plants it under the family's plum tree, where it glows on dark nights.

fail.log: Nobody is left of that sect. You keep the pearl in the end, with a quiet apology to the silk.

events.text: The hunger has turned. It is no longer asking. It is taking: from your own qi, your own strength, a little each night, the way a cold house takes the heat out of a sleeper.

choices.text: Go and find a fight, any fight

ok.log: A bandit on the north road is the first fool you meet. The hunger pounces. For one night you sleep warm.

fail.log: You are too weak to win even this. You crawl back to your room, and the hunger takes the difference from you. (-10 health)

effects.log: You sit through the nights, watching it feed on you, refusing to feed it on anyone else. You learn the exact shape of your own life, by losing pieces of it. (-6 health)

choices.text: Sell your best coat for a beast core

effects.log: A hunter trades you a beast core for your coat and a few coins. It is a cold walk home with a warm stone in your pocket.

events.text: Your hair is thinning. Your hands shake in the mornings. People who have not seen you in a year ask if you have been ill. The voice has stopped making jokes.

choices.text: Ask the voice to talk to you anyway

effects.log: It talks, haltingly, about the best meals it ever had. It is like listening to a starving person read a menu. You both feel better, a little.

choices.text: Go and sit by a friendly hearth for a while

effects.log: Someone feeds you soup and does not ask questions. The hunger does not touch the people of the house. It never has. It sits by the fire with you, sullen.

events.text: In the worst of the starving, you find yourself standing outside a sleeping village at midnight, with no memory of walking there. Every lamp-lit window is a meal.

effects.log: You turn round. Each step away is like walking into wind. At dawn you are on a hilltop, alone, shaking, clean. (-6 health)

choices.text: Go into the hills and hunt a beast instead

ok.log: You find a bear in the high woods and beat it, and the warm, wild beast-qi fills you up. You go home past the village and every window is just a window again.

fail.log: The bear wins. You limp back past the village at dawn, too hurt to be hungry. It is a kind of mercy. (-12 health)

events.text: A Buddhist nun finds you collapsed outside a temple gate in the snow. She takes one look at you and says, "Ah. One of the hungry ones. We get one every hundred years or so."

choices.text: Stay the winter at the temple

effects.log: The nun feeds you plain rice and plainer chanting. The chanting, somehow, feeds the other hunger too. By spring you can stand straight.

choices.text: Ask what happened to the last one

effects.log: "Ate a general," she says. "Then a city. Then nothing, because there was no one left who would fight it." She pours tea. "You look like you would rather not."

events.text: A famine year. No beasts in the hills, no bandits on the roads, only hungry people. Your hunger is starving too, and so is everyone you meet.

choices.text: Share your rice and starve both ways

effects.log: You give your rice away. You starve twice over, in the belly and below it. People in that village remember your face for the rest of their lives. (-8 health)

choices.text: Hunt the bandits who are hoarding grain

ok.log: You find the hoarders' barn and its guards. The guards fall, their qi comes to you, and the grain goes back to the village. A rare year where hunger and justice go the same way.

fail.log: There are too many of them. You stagger away with nothing. The village eats bark. (-12 health)

events.text: You count your grey hairs in a bowl of water. There are more than there should be. The System, when you ask, says quietly: "Years. When I starve, I eat years. I am sorry, host. I do not choose it."

effects.log: "I know you do not choose it," you say. It is quiet a long time. "Thank you," it says. It has never said that either.

choices.text: Vow to never let it get this bad again

effects.log: You make a plan: a fight a season, a treasure a year, points saved for feasts. The voice helps with the arithmetic, eagerly.

events.text: In the starving year a wandering sect elder with a sly face offers you a deal: a beast core every month, if you fight whoever the elder points at. No questions.

effects.log: The elder shrugs and finds someone else. You hear a year later that the someone else is a wanted killer now. You are glad, and hungry.

roll.foeName: A merchant guard the elder points at

ok.log: You beat the guard. The elder pays. You find out later that the merchant was honest and the elder was robbing them. You take the core and you walk away and you do not go back.

fail.log: The guard is better than you. The elder pays you nothing and laughs. (-10 health)

events.text: You are hungry, not yet starving, and you know what is coming. A wise host feeds before the starving, not after. The voice clears its throat.

ok.log: A season in the high woods, beast by beast. You come back brown and lean and the hunger is calm.

fail.log: The wolves are clever. You come back with scars and not much else. (-8 health)

effects.log: You count the points in the ledger and do sums by lamplight. The voice approves, as a clerk approves of a careful household.

choices.text: Go to a quiet mountain and eat nothing

effects.log: You go to the mountain and sit. You are proving something. You are not sure what, or to whom.

events.text: After the worst year, you wake one morning and the hunger is quiet. Not sated: sleeping. You walk to the river, and the light on the water is just light, and the people at the ferry are just people.

choices.text: Sit by the river all day

effects.log: You sit until sundown. It is the best day of the decade. You do not try to explain it to anyone.
You train like a person, not a mouth. It is slower. It is yours. It is wonderful.

events.text: A child in your village, who has always liked you, brings you a bowl of rice and says you look like a ghost. The hunger, for a moment, looks at the child.

choices.text: Take the bowl and send the child home

effects.log: You thank the child and close the door and sit with your back against it until the moment passes. The rice is the best thing you have ever eaten.

choices.text: Tell the voice, out loud, never

effects.log: "Never," you say. The child thinks you mean the rice. The voice knows. It does not ask again, not about children, not ever.

events.text: You beat a young swordsman in a duel they started. As they fall, their qi lifts toward you, and you see it is thin, scraped together over years of rice-and-water training. They have nothing else.

effects.log: You close your hand. The light sinks back into them. They stare at you, then bow lower than anyone has ever bowed to you.
You take it. They will recover, slowly, if they can afford good rice. You do not know if they can.

events.text: A tiger has been killing cattle in the valley. You find it in its den: an old tigress, too slow to hunt deer any more, three cubs behind her.

choices.text: Drive her into the deep forest

ok.log: You chase her, unhurt, deeper into the forest than the village will ever go, with the cubs tumbling after. The cattle killing stops. The hunger is very confused.

fail.log: She fights you before she runs. You take a swipe across the arm and let her go. She does not come back to the valley. (-8 health)

choices.text: Fight her and devour her qi

ok.log: She falls, and her fierce old qi comes to you like heat off a stone. She gets up, slow and diminished, and leads the cubs away. The village cheers. You do not, quite.

fail.log: She is old, but she is a tiger. You leave the den on your own feet, barely. (-12 health)

events.text: A defeated bandit begs you, on their knees: "Not my qi. Please. I have a sick mother. It is the only thing that lets me carry sacks at the docks."

effects.log: You let them go. Next year you pass the docks and there they are, carrying sacks. They wave. You never find out whether the mother was real.
Half, and a lecture about honest work. They are grateful in a sour, complicated way.

events.text: {npc}, a gentle monk who heals the poor, comes to you and says, "I know what you are. Will you let me show you something?" {He} takes you to a ward full of sick people. "Their qi is weak. Yours is overflowing."

choices.text: Give some of your qi to the sick

effects.log: You go from bed to bed with {npc}, a little light from your palm to each chest. The hunger is appalled. By evening the ward is warmer, and so, oddly, are you. (-12 qi)

choices.text: Say you have nothing to spare

effects.log: {npc} nods without judgement. "Next year, then," {he} says, and pours you tea, and you wish {he} had argued.

events.text: You have been giving qi away in {npc}'s ward every year. The hunger, you notice, has changed. It still wants. But it has learned, somehow, that the giving makes the next meal taste sweeter.

effects.log: "It is like a river," {npc} says. "Water that never leaves a lake goes bad." You give, and fill, and give. (-8 qi)
"I had a hungry brother once," {npc} says. "Nobody showed my brother a ward." {He} does not say more. You do not ask.

events.text: The raider chief whose name you have hated for years lies beaten at your feet, at last. Everything he took could be yours, and more: every year of his long, cruel cultivation. The hunger is singing.

effects.log: You take everything. He is left an ordinary old man with an ordinary old man's strength, sitting in the dust. It is not as sweet as you dreamed. Revenge rarely is.

choices.text: Leave him with his strength and his shame

effects.log: You turn your back. He has to live now, beaten, known, in front of everyone. The hunger screams for a month. The villages he burned, you think, would have understood.
Justice that is not yours, again. Slow, dull, fair. The hunger thinks you are mad. You sleep well.

events.text: A young fighter, who cannot be more than fifteen, challenges you to prove themselves. They are terrible. They are very, very brave.

effects.log: You fall over rather convincingly. The young fighter is radiant. Your voice says, with deep disgust, that you have no sense of dinner.

ok.log: You put them on the ground without a bruise and spend the afternoon fixing their stance. You take nothing. They come back every spring.

fail.log: They get one lucky hit in. You are so proud of them you forget to be annoyed. (-3 health)

events.text: Ding. The System asks a question it has never asked before: "Host. Why do you let them go? I have been doing the sums for years. It never pays."

choices.text: Say it pays in a different coin

effects.log: "What coin?" it asks. You try to explain: a village that waves, a bandit at the docks, sleeping at night. It listens. "I will open a new column," it says at last.

choices.text: Say because you are not only a hunger

effects.log: "No," it agrees, after a long time. "You are not. I am glad, I think. I am not sure. I will tell you when I am."

events.text: An enemy who has hunted you for years lies wounded after a landslide, pinned and helpless. Their qi is strong. Nobody would ever know.

effects.log: You dig with your hands for an hour. They do not thank you. They do not hunt you again, either. (-6 health)

choices.text: Dig them out, and take a fee in qi

effects.log: You dig them out and then take a little, openly, eye to eye. "For the trouble," you say. They nod, as if that were fair. Maybe it is.

events.text: An arrogant young master of a great clan, with eight bodyguards and a fan, decides that you looked at his sister. "Kneel," he says, "and I will only break one leg."

ok.log: He goes down. His proud, pampered qi flows to you, rich as temple cake. His eight bodyguards look at each other and quietly decide to find new jobs.

fail.log: He is better trained than he is wise. You get a beating and he gets a story. (-10 health)

effects.log: You kneel. He leaves, satisfied. The voice writes him down under a heading called Later.

events.text: The young master is back, with his clan's elder this time. "This is the one," he says. The elder looks at you, a little bored, and then, as the hunger looks back at the elder, not bored at all.

ok.log: The elder falls. A deep old stream of qi follows. The young master's fan drops from his hand. In the genre, this is called face-slapping. The voice calls it lunch.

fail.log: The elder is the real thing. You escape, and the young master tells this story for the rest of his life. (-14 health)

effects.log: The elder accepts, gravely, and then takes the young master by the ear and leaves. You hear him being scolded down the street.

events.text: At the sect entrance trial everyone calls you trash: weak roots, no family, no master. Your opponent, a rich clan's daughter, does not even draw.

ok.log: The trash wins. Her clan qi, rich with ginseng and good teachers, flows to you in a bright stream. The examiners sit up. The genre is satisfied.

fail.log: She draws, after all, and that is that. The voice says next year, next year, very firmly. (-6 health)

choices.text: Lose on purpose to stay hidden

effects.log: You lose, and nobody looks at you twice. Hidden power is a trope too. The voice is annoyed but admits the strategy has merit.

events.text: You fall off a cliff. Of course you do. At the bottom there is a cave. Of course there is. In the cave, glowing on a stone shelf, there is a beast core, left by something old and long gone.

effects.log: You take the core and climb out, bruised, laughing at how predictable heaven is. The voice approves of heaven's predictability. (-5 health)
You eat it in the cave, sitting on the cold stone, and the warmth carries you all the way up the cliff. (-5 health)

events.text: A beautiful old manual turns up at the market, called the Heaven-Devouring Demonic Scripture. The seller swears it is genuine. The voice reads two lines over your shoulder and says, "Amateurs."

effects.log: You read it in the evenings. It is ninety pages of very confident nonsense and one page that is, unexpectedly, quite good. The voice will not tell you which.

choices.text: Warn the seller what happens to people who carry it

effects.log: The seller packs up quickly. Orthodox inspectors come through the market the next day and find nothing. The seller sends you a jar of pickles.

events.text: A tournament is offering a Thousand-Year Spirit Fruit to the winner. Every hungry cultivator in the land is coming. Your voice is practically vibrating.

ok.log: You win, fight by fight, each one a meal, and at the end they hand you a fruit that glows like a lantern. The voice composes a short poem about it.

fail.log: You reach the final and lose. Still, it was a feast on the way up. The voice calls it a very good buffet with a disappointing dessert. (-12 health)

choices.text: Watch from the stands and learn

effects.log: You watch every bout and learn every style without eating any of them. It is strange, learning the slow way. Your notes are very good.

events.text: An old man in a teahouse spills tea on you, apologises, and says, in passing: "Your hunger has a crack in it. Here, and here." He taps two points on your arm. Nobody else hears.

choices.text: Ask the old man to teach you

effects.log: He laughs, says he is only a tea merchant, and teaches you three breaths that close the cracks. When you look up, his seat is empty and the bill is paid.

ok.log: You follow him to a bamboo grove, where he turns and says you are rude, but persistent. He gives you one piece of advice: never eat when angry. You never forget it.

fail.log: You turn a corner and he is simply gone. The voice says it never smelled any qi on him at all, which is the most frightening thing it has ever said.

events.text: A hidden master, disguised as the sect's cook, has been watching you for years. Tonight the cook stands in your doorway with a ladle and says: "Your hunger. Show me."

ok.log: You let the hunger reach toward the cook, and it touches something like a mountain, and recoils. The cook nods. "Good. It knows fear. Then it can be taught." Lessons begin that week, over the stew pot.

fail.log: The cook taps your forehead with the ladle and you sit down hard. "Not yet," says the cook, and leaves you a bowl of stew. (-6 health)

choices.text: Offer the cook some tea instead

effects.log: The cook laughs and drinks the tea and talks about soup for an hour. You are sure you learned something, but you are not sure what.

events.text: Ding. A new screen opens. SUGGESTED QUEST: DEFEAT THE BANDIT KING OF RED CLIFF. REWARD: DELICIOUS. The voice admits, when pressed, that it wrote the reward line itself.

roll.foeName: The Bandit King of Red Cliff

ok.log: The Bandit King falls, and his qi really is delicious: wild, smoky, a bit of everything he ever stole. The villages pay you in rice and taels and gratitude.

fail.log: The Bandit King is called a king for a reason. You come home with nothing but the reward line, still reading DELICIOUS, mocking you. (-14 health)

choices.text: Tell it to write honest quest text

effects.log: REWARD: SOMEWHAT DELICIOUS, the screen now reads. You give up.

events.text: A proud clan that turns away anyone with weak roots is holding a grand banquet. You are a realm higher than any of them now. The invitation is clearly meant to be an insult.

effects.log: You go. You are polite and calm and very obviously stronger than anyone in the hall. Nobody slaps any faces. Everyone feels slapped. It is the best banquet of your life.
You do not go. They wait for you all evening. You hear the next day that the empty seat was all anyone talked about.

events.text: You meet another host whose System is not hungry at all: it signs in, every year, and pays them in rice cakes. Your voice is quiet for a while, and then says, with real bitterness, "Rice cakes."

effects.log: The other host is so serene it is unbearable. Your voice sulks the whole time. You like them very much.

choices.text: Ask your voice if it is jealous

effects.log: "I am a great appetite," it says. "I am not jealous of a clerk with a stamp." Then, later: "Do you think they were good rice cakes?"

events.text: A beast tide pours out of the deep mountains toward the border towns, thousands of maddened spirit beasts. For every other cultivator it is a catastrophe. For you it is, the voice says, trying not to sound happy, "a buffet".

ok.log: You hold the pass for three days. Wild beast-qi pours into you from every side, and at the end the alpha falls and leaves a core the size of a fist. The towns name a gate after you.

fail.log: You hold for a day before the tide pushes you back. The towns are saved by the army, and by the day you bought them. (-16 health)

effects.log: You carry children and grandmothers out over the hills. You eat nothing all week. The voice, astonishingly, does not complain once.

events.text: Deep in a forbidden ruin you find an ancient stone tablet: the record of the last host of a devouring System, a thousand years ago. The last line reads only: IT WAS NEVER FULL.

effects.log: It is the story of a host who ate a kingdom and was still hungry. In the margins, scratched later, in another hand: but I was. Once. A spring day. You read that line many times.

choices.text: Ask your voice if it remembers

effects.log: "I remember a spring day," it says, slowly. "Someone fed a bird, and I was full, and I did not know why." It is quiet the rest of the year.

events.text: Somewhere, the old prophecy says, a Heaven-Devouring Demon will be born and swallow the martial world. You are beginning to suspect the prophecy means you. The voice is suspiciously silent on the subject.

choices.text: Decide to prove the prophecy wrong

effects.log: Prophecies are just old men's fears with good handwriting. You will be the devourer who did not swallow the world. It is a good enough ambition for one life.
If they are going to fear you anyway, you might as well be worth fearing. The voice says nothing. It is, you think, slightly afraid of you now.

events.text: Ten. You have devoured ten fighters, and the System marks it with a sound like a temple gong. Your bones feel heavier and surer. You lie awake trying to remember all ten faces.

effects.log: You remember eight. The voice supplies the other two, with a short review of each. You keep the list.
You buy a skewer of grilled meat and a cup of tea and toast yourselves on a roof. The voice makes a speech. It is far too long.

events.text: Thirty. The gong sounds again, and this time something enormous settles into you: years. Ten more of them. You will live longer than you were born to. It is very quiet in your head afterwards.

effects.log: "Nobody's," the voice says. "Everybody's. A little from each. Nobody misses a day, I promise. Or almost nobody."
You make a list of things to do with ten extra years. It starts with seeing the sea and ends with being kind to someone hungry.

events.text: One hundred. The System does not sound a gong this time. It is quiet, and then it says, very simply: "I know what they knew now. All of them. Do you want to hear it?"

effects.log: A hundred lives' worth of tricks, fears, small joys. You learn that the bandit chief from your youth loved his goats. You learn more than you wanted to and exactly enough.
"They are yours as much as mine," it says. "But I will keep them. Somebody should."

events.text: A sated year. The hunger is curled up somewhere under your ribs like a cat on a warm floor. Everything is bright and easy, and you find you are kinder to people than usual.

effects.log: You travel round your old haunts, buying people dinner. Nobody asks why you are so cheerful. You could not have told them.
With the hunger asleep, your own qi runs like a clear stream. You make more progress in a season than in a year.

events.text: You are sated, and the voice is being philosophical about it. "Host," it says, "if I am full, am I still me? I am a hunger. A full hunger is a contradiction."

effects.log: "You are a friend who likes dinner," you say. It thinks about this for a long time and decides it can live with it.
"Perhaps," it says, and yawns, which a voice should not be able to do, and goes quiet for a week.

events.text: A young disciple of another school asks, very nervously, how you grew so strong so fast. Thirty fights of other people's qi are humming in your veins.

effects.log: "I won a lot," you say, "and I kept a little of everyone I beat." The disciple thinks it is a metaphor. In a way, it is.
The disciple nods earnestly and goes off to train harder. Your voice says this is the most shameless thing you have ever done.

events.text: With a hundred devoured, there are fighters who cross the road when they see you. Children hide behind their parents. A great sect sends a polite letter asking you to please not visit.

effects.log: You arrive with a gift of tea and do not fight anyone. The sect is so relieved it throws a banquet. The voice wants to eat the banquet. You do not let it.

choices.text: Live quietly in the mountains a while

effects.log: You find a hut and a stream and a few years of quiet. The fear in the world settles, slowly, like silt.

events.text: You count, one evening, how many you have refused. It is more than the number you devoured. You did not expect that. Neither, it seems, did the voice.

effects.log: "I know," it says. "I keep both columns." It says it the way a clerk says a ledger balances: quietly proud.
You keep it like a stone in your pocket, to turn over on bad days.

events.text: You have a beast core in your pack, warm as a hearthstone. You could use it for strength, the ordinary way, or let the System devour it whole. The voice is being very patient about it.

effects.log: The core melts into red-gold light and runs up your arm like warm water. The hunger lies down and purrs.

choices.text: Keep it for a lean year

effects.log: You wrap it in cloth and put it away. The voice checks on it every night, like a child checking on a cake in an oven.

events.text: A hunter has a beast core for sale, freshly taken from a mountain boar that will, the hunter swears, recover nicely. The price is fair. The voice is begging.

effects.log: You buy it. The hunter throws in a strip of jerky. The voice ignores the jerky completely.
You walk on. The voice says nothing, eloquently, all the way to the next town.

events.text: An Essence Pearl is up for auction at a merchant guild. The bidding is fierce. Every hungry cultivator in the city is in the room, and so, unfortunately, are you.

effects.log: You win at forty taels. The room glares at you. The voice glows so happily you are afraid someone will see it.
A fat merchant wins it and puts it in a jar on a shelf, to look at. The voice is in mourning for a week.

ok.log: You catch the winner, a nervous merchant, and talk them into selling it on for half the price, in exchange for an introduction to a sect elder. Everyone wins.

fail.log: The winner thinks you are a thief and calls the guard. You spend an evening explaining.

events.text: You hold an Essence Pearl in your hand. Use it, and your mind sharpens. Devour it, and something of the master whose essence it holds becomes part of you, along with three more years.

effects.log: The pearl dissolves into silver light. You feel, for a moment, an old master's patience settle in behind your eyes. It stays.
You put it away for a worse year. The voice says you are a very responsible host and also a coward.

events.text: {npc}, a friend of yours, has a child dying of a qi sickness. The physician says only a beast core's essence could steady the child's channels. You have one in your pack. The hunger has been eyeing it for a month.

choices.text: Give the core to the child

effects.log: You give it. The physician grinds it into a tonic and the child sleeps easily for the first time in weeks. The hunger cries, quietly, like a disappointed dog. You pat your own chest, absurdly, to comfort it.

ok.log: A herbalist two valleys over has exactly the root. The child lives and you keep the core. Some years heaven is kind to everyone.

fail.log: You search, and fail, and come back, and give the core anyway. It is late, but not too late. (-4 health)
